title: C498 — Left rear lamp connector reference
introduction:
I read this reference like a seating chart for the left rear lamp: the drawing locates a cavity, and its matching table row explains the circuit’s job. Start with the connector identification table, compare the housing outline, then follow the cavity label into the pin assignments. The park, stop/turn and ground descriptions help distinguish connections that share the same housing.

This page supports identification and circuit lookup. It does not teach connector access, probing, testing or replacement. The physical viewing direction, gauge convention and meanings of the Size and Used codes are not defined here; keep those entries as reference data rather than turning them into workshop instructions.

edits.why: I use the housing details to navigate the drawing: the projecting housing feature sits to the left of the illustrated face, with smaller projections along the right edge. Those landmarks help distinguish the drawing’s sides without assuming how the connector faces when installed. The shaded cavities correspond to rows with blank circuit descriptions; shading is not an electrical test result.

Match the drawing’s cavity label to the Cavity column, then read across for Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function and Terminal Part Number. Inboard, middle and outboard distinguish the stop/turn functions within the lamp. Keep the park description’s alternative wording and the turn-signal output’s opposite-side wording intact: a function label alone does not establish the wire’s route or explain that cross-side relationship. Blank circuit fields provide no circuit assignment.

The Engineering Shell entry connects this service-parts row to the housing identity above. Number, Service Part and Image are separate lookup fields; the image filename is not another connector-face illustration. The material and gauge entries describe the listed service part, without supplying a wire-selection, terminal-repair or installation procedure.
